titre: A greenfield migration to S/4HANA, from A to Z
intro: The six SAP Activate phases on a timeline. Click a bar, a quality gate or the go-live to open the details.

exemple.description: Calvane (fictional), pump manufacturer, 3 plants, in-house ERP replaced by S/4HANA

chronologieAria: Greenfield project timeline: SAP Activate phases, steps and quality gates from M-15 to M+2
enContinu: governance, Clean Core, risks, change management
causesTitre: The 5 most common causes of failure
causes: Fit-to-standard that copies the old system
note: Typical approach and indicative durations for a medium scope, to be adapted to each program. Discover takes place before the project starts.

s1.obj: Decide why to move to S/4HANA, with which approach and which deployment model.
act: Value analysis: processes to improve, cost of the current landscape
Choosing the approach: greenfield, brownfield or bluefield
Choosing the deployment: public cloud, private cloud (RISE) or on-premise
Discovering the solution: trial system, demonstrations
pre: Inventory of the current landscape: systems, custom code, data
s1.ex: Calvane runs on a 20-year-old in-house ERP, with hundreds of custom objects nobody masters any more. Carrying the existing system over makes no sense: greenfield. S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition via RISE is chosen. Budget of €9M, go-live targeted for April 1, as a big bang across the three plants.
ai: Analyze the current landscape (custom code, actual transaction usage) to measure complexity
Process mining to measure the current processes
r: Vague business case, 'we have to migrate': no criteria to arbitrate afterwards
Quantified objectives: lead times, costs, quality
Approach chosen on license cost alone: the transformation is underestimated
Compare the full cost, change management included
Big bang chosen without risk analysis: cutover too heavy
Compare big bang and phased deployment before deciding

s2.obj: Get the project up and running.
act: Governance: steering committee, design authority, change board
s2.ex: Calvane chooses an integrator on a fixed price per phase. Monthly steering committee, weekly design authority. Six process owners named (purchasing, production, sales, finance, logistics, maintenance), each with two part-time key users.
r: Key users 'in their spare time': workshops with no decision-makers
Their time reserved in writing, backfill in their job
Unclear client and integrator roles: gray areas
RACI signed by both parties
Fixed price signed on a still-unknown scope: disputes
Fixed price per phase, Explore scoped separately

s3.s: An S/4HANA ready for the workshops
s3.obj: Have an S/4HANA system with standard content to show the processes to the business.
act: Providing the reference system (starter) and the DEV / QAS / PRD landscape
liv: Reference system with standard processes and sample data
s3.ex: The reference system is delivered in six weeks, with standard processes pre-activated and demo data. It will serve for all the Explore workshops.
s3.own: Technical team, hosting provider or SAP (RISE)
r: System delivered late: workshops on PowerPoint
Order it as soon as the contract is signed
Empty system, no content or data: abstract workshops
Activate the best practices and load sample data

s4.obj: Set the ground rules early for data, interfaces, testing, extensions and change management.
act: Migration strategy: which data to carry over, and which to leave behind
pre: Map of the current landscape: systems, interfaces, volumes
liv: Strategy documents validated by the design authority
s4.ex: Calvane carries over only master data and open items: open orders, stock, open accounting items. History stays accessible in an archive. 42 interfaces to rebuild. Clean Core rule: no modification of the standard.
ai: Mapping interfaces and volumes from the logs
s4.own: Architects and the lead of each stream
r: Data strategy postponed: cleansing started too late
Decide in Prepare what is carried over
Clean Core rule not written down: standard modified in Realize
Formalize it and have the design authority validate it

q1.obj: Authorize the start of Explore: team, system and ground rules in place.
act: Review of the organization, governance and strategies
q1.ex: Gate passed with one condition: the maintenance key user is only 20% available. The plant director commits to freeing them up before the first workshop.
ai: Consolidating the status of the criteria
r: Explore started without key users available: empty workshops
Make this criterion blocking at the gate

s5.s: Show the standard, decide process by process
s5.obj: Show the SAP standard to the business and decide, process by process, whether to adopt it.
act: Demonstrating standard processes on the reference system
Prioritizing and building the gap backlog
pre: Process owners and key users present and empowered to decide
s5.ex: 85 workshops over twelve weeks. The standard covers 82% of needs. 140 gaps raised, 60 dropped after discussion: 'we've done it this way for 20 years' is not enough to justify a gap.
ai: Compare actual processes (process mining) to the standard
Workshop minutes and backlog generated automatically
r: Workshops turned into collecting the old system's requirements: massive custom code
Start from the standard, justify every gap
Decision-makers absent: decisions challenged later
The process owner signs each process
Explore drags on: Realize squeezed
Time-boxed workshops, standard by default if no decision

s6.s: How to deliver each gap, Clean Core
s6.obj: Describe how each retained gap will be delivered, in line with Clean Core.
act: Choosing the technique: configuration, key user extension, BTP extension, ABAP Cloud
s6.ex: 80 gaps retained: 35 in configuration, 20 in key user extensions, 15 developments on BTP, 10 forms. No modification of the standard.
ai: Suggesting the Clean Core-compatible extension technique
r: Vague specifications: a build that fumbles
Standard format with acceptance criteria
Extensions outside Clean Core: costly upgrades
Blocking design authority
Optimistic estimates: Realize undersized
Estimate by benchmarks, with a margin

s7.s: What to migrate, how each flow works
s7.obj: Define which data to migrate, with which rules, and how each interface works.
act: List of data objects: materials, suppliers, customers, bills of materials
Mapping rules between the old and the new
Launching the cleansing in the legacy system
s7.ex: 38 objects to migrate. Of 25,000 materials, 9,000 have been inactive for five years and will not be carried over. Suppliers and customers become Business Partners.
ai: Data profiling: duplicates, inactive records, inconsistent fields
s7.own: Data owners, migration team, integration architect
r: Cleansing left to Realize: too late
Start it in Explore
Rules written by IT alone: wrong business rules
The data owner validates every rule

q2.obj: Authorize the build: scope decided, designed and estimated.
act: Review of the designs and the Realize estimate
pre: Designs approved by the design authority
q2.ex: Eight gaps remain open. They are listed with a deadline: without a decision by sprint 2, the standard applies.
ai: Consolidating the status of the backlog
r: Realize launched with open gaps: scope drifts
List of open gaps, deadline and default decision

s8.obj: Build the solution in short iterations, shown to the business at the end of each sprint.
act: Demonstration to key users at the end of the sprint
pre: Key users available for the demonstrations
s8.ex: Eight three-week sprints. At each demonstration, about 15% of the topics are adjusted: that many defects avoided at acceptance.
r: Demonstrations skipped: surprises at acceptance
Demonstration mandatory at every sprint
Untracked changes in requirements: drift
Everything goes through the change board

s9.s: Develop the gaps, rebuild the flows
s9.obj: Develop the retained gaps and rebuild the interfaces.
act: Developments on BTP and in ABAP Cloud
s9.ex: 42 interfaces rebuilt. The carrier and the bank provide their test environments a month late: the risk is tracked in committee from the first week.
r: Dependence on third parties: interfaces impossible to test
Third-party schedules written into their contracts
Code outside Clean Core rules: technical debt
Automatic code checks (ATC)

s10.obj: Load correct and complete data within the planned time.
act: Three to four mock loads with the Migration Cockpit
s10.ex: Load 1: 18% rejects. Load 2: 6%. Load 3: 1%. The full load takes 30 hours, for a 72-hour cutover window.
r: First load too late: late discoveries
First load at the start of Realize
Token business validation: errors in production
Data owner sign-off per object

s11.s: End to end, with real data
s11.obj: Prove that the solution works end to end, with real data and the real roles.
s11.ex: 450 scenarios. 600 defects found over two SIT cycles. Six weeks of acceptance, signed off with 12 minor defects open.
r: Testing compressed to hit the date: defects in production
Testing duration protected in the schedule
Authorizations tested last: users blocked at go-live
Test with the real roles from SIT

s12.obj: Prepare every user for the new system and, above all, for the new processes.
s12.ex: 1,200 users, 180 roles. 40 key users train their colleagues over six weeks. The heaviest changes: production planning and time entry.
ai: Materials and work instructions by role
r: Training on the tool only, not on the processes: rejection
Train by business scenario
Training too early: forgotten by go-live
Train two to four weeks before

q3.obj: Authorize the final preparation: the solution is tested and the data is ready.
pre: Loads within quality and duration thresholds
q3.ex: Zero blocking defects, 1% rejects on the last load. Move into Deploy authorized.
r: Defects downgraded to minor to pass the gate
Severity arbitrated by the business

s13.obj: Prepare the cutover minute by minute, then rehearse it.
act: Closing and shutting down the old system
s13.ex: Runbook of 640 tasks. First rehearsal: 81 hours, too long. Second rehearsal: 64 hours after optimization, within the 72-hour window.
ai: Runbook consistency check: dependencies, durations, omissions
r: No full rehearsal: the cutover overruns the window
At least one timed rehearsal
Poorly prepared closing of the old system: wrong opening balance
Finance in the runbook, with its controls

s14.obj: Decide, on criteria written in advance, whether to cut over.
act: Review of criteria: testing, data, training, support, runbook
pre: Criteria defined and signed in advance
s14.ex: 22 criteria: 20 green, 2 amber (30 night-team users not yet trained, a customs interface under correction). Go with reservations, each with an owner.
r: Pressure of the date: go despite red criteria
Criteria set in advance, not renegotiable in the meeting
Reservations not followed: incidents from day one
Each reservation has an owner and a date

s15.obj: Cut over and start operations on S/4HANA.
pre: Cutover and support teams in place
s15.ex: Old ERP shut down Thursday evening. Load, reconciliation of stock and accounting balances. Opening Monday, April 1 at 6 am.
ai: Real-time monitoring of flows and gaps
r: Reconciliation skipped to save time: invisible gaps
Reconciliation mandatory before opening
Fallback decided too late
Fallback criteria set before the point of no return

s16.s: Stabilize, get through the first closing
s16.obj: Stabilize the system and support the first month-end closing.
s16.ex: Eight weeks of hypercare. Peak of 400 tickets in the first week. First closing takes 7 days instead of 5; the target is met at the second.
r: Experts released too early: incidents unanswered
Team locked until exit
First closing not prepared: financial delay
Closing rehearsal before go-live

q4.obj: Close the project and confirm that run can take over alone.
act: Review of the handover to run
q4.ex: Exit declared ten weeks after go-live. 15 minor tickets formally taken over by run.
r: Closure with open incidents: run inherits a debt
List of incidents formally taken over

s17.obj: Keep the solution alive and benefit from new SAP capabilities.
s17.ex: First upgrade ten months after go-live, done in three weeks thanks to Clean Core.
ai: Analyzing actual usage to prioritize improvements
r: Custom code accumulating after go-live: difficult upgrades
Keep the design authority going after the project

transverse.obj: Run the program end to end: decide fast, arbitrate cleanly, bring the business along.
act: Steering committee: arbitration, quality gates, go / no-go
Design authority: Clean Core and solution consistency
Change board: every change to scope, schedule or budget
pre: Roles and bodies defined from Prepare
transverse.ex: Monthly steering committee, then weekly for the last three months. 25 risks tracked; three turned red: key user availability, third-party environments, cutover duration.
ai: Caution: client data only in a tool approved by the client
r: Committees that observe without deciding
Every committee ends with traced decisions
Indicators green, reality red: the watermelon effect
Quantified alert thresholds and checks on the ground
